question: In an asset renewal strategy, what does a risk based priority list mainly combine?
correctAnswer: Likelihood of failure with consequence of failure for each asset
explanation: Risk based renewal ranks assets by how likely failure is and how serious the result would be, rather than by age or cost alone.
options: Original purchase price with the year the asset was installed
Likelihood of failure with consequence of failure for each asset
Pipe material type with the size of the crew available nearby
Number of past work orders with the age of the water in the main
optionA: Original purchase price with the year the asset was installed
optionB: Likelihood of failure with consequence of failure for each asset
optionC: Pipe material type with the size of the crew available nearby
optionD: Number of past work orders with the age of the water in the main
sourceReference: Supporting topic reference: Asset Renewal Strategy. See README for source scope and limitations.

question: What is the first step in a system wide water quality risk assessment?
correctAnswer: Identify hazards and hazardous events across the whole system
explanation: A risk assessment starts by identifying hazards and the events that could introduce them, before controls and priorities are set.
options: Set a higher booster dose at every storage facility in the system
Rank the next five years of capital projects by their total cost
Identify hazards and hazardous events across the whole system
Collect the complaint records from the largest pressure zone first
optionA: Set a higher booster dose at every storage facility in the system
optionB: Rank the next five years of capital projects by their total cost
optionC: Identify hazards and hazardous events across the whole system
optionD: Collect the complaint records from the largest pressure zone first

options: Expected retirements, system growth and required certifications
The average age of the fleet vehicles used by field crews each year
The number of customer accounts that pay their bills online monthly
Past spending on office supplies and contracted cleaning services

question: What is a district metered area mainly used to track in a metering strategy?
correctAnswer: Flows into a defined zone to locate losses and demand patterns
explanation: A district metered area measures flow into a bounded zone, which helps locate losses and understand demand in that area.
options: Chlorine decay inside a single storage tank over one summer season
The pressure setting chosen for one pressure reducing valve station
Staff travel time between the office and the farthest sampling site

question: What is the main purpose of pressure management in a distribution system?
correctAnswer: Keep pressures in a planned range while reducing excess pressure
explanation: Pressure management keeps service pressures adequate while trimming excess pressure that drives leakage and stress on pipes.
options: Raise pressure at night so storage tanks refill as fast as possible
Hold one fixed pressure at every point in the system at all times
Keep pressures in a planned range while reducing excess pressure
Lower pressure below the planned range during every peak demand period
optionA: Raise pressure at night so storage tanks refill as fast as possible
optionB: Hold one fixed pressure at every point in the system at all times
optionC: Keep pressures in a planned range while reducing excess pressure
optionD: Lower pressure below the planned range during every peak demand period

question: What should an intermunicipal supply agreement clearly define?

Which utility hosts the annual operator appreciation event each year
The brand of meters each utility installs on new residential services

The cost of printing and mailing the annual water quality report
Short term overtime that is recovered in the same operating month
Planned renewal work and unexpected major repairs over time

question: When benchmarking performance, why do utilities normalize results by system size?
correctAnswer: So systems of different scales can be compared more fairly
explanation: Normalizing by measures such as length of main or volume supplied makes comparisons fairer between systems of different sizes.

So systems of different scales can be compared more fairly
So each system can report results without sharing its raw data
So small systems can skip reporting results in low demand years

question: Which factor can raise a main renewal priority even when its break history is low?
correctAnswer: A high consequence of failure at a critical customer it serves
explanation: Consequence matters as well as likelihood, so a main serving a critical customer can rank high even with few past breaks.
options: A high consequence of failure at a critical customer it serves
A low material cost for the pipe that was originally installed
A wide road allowance that makes excavation easier for the crew
A recent hydrant inspection program completed on the same street

question: Which condition most increases concern about nitrification in a chloraminated area?
correctAnswer: Long water age with warm temperatures and a fading disinfectant residual
explanation: Warm, aged water with a declining residual gives nitrifying bacteria favourable conditions, so those areas need closer attention.
options: Short water age with cold temperatures and a stable disinfectant residual
High turnover in storage with steady temperatures through the whole season
Frequent flushing at dead ends combined with a well maintained residual
Long water age with warm temperatures and a fading disinfectant residual
optionA: Short water age with cold temperatures and a stable disinfectant residual
optionB: High turnover in storage with steady temperatures through the whole season
optionC: Frequent flushing at dead ends combined with a well maintained residual
optionD: Long water age with warm temperatures and a fading disinfectant residual
sourceTitle: US EPA - Small Drinking Water Systems Handbook

question: Two of five operators retire within 18 months and one vacancy has been hard to fill. What is the best first workforce planning action?
correctAnswer: Build a hiring and training timeline that staggers recruitment ahead of the retirements
explanation: Starting recruitment and training early, staggered against the retirement dates, protects qualified coverage and allows overlap for handover.
options: Wait until both retirements take effect, then advertise both positions at the same time
Build a hiring and training timeline that staggers recruitment ahead of the retirements
Reduce sampling and flushing schedules so the remaining operators can cover all other work
Assign the retiring operators extra overtime so no new hiring is needed before they leave
optionA: Wait until both retirements take effect, then advertise both positions at the same time
optionB: Build a hiring and training timeline that staggers recruitment ahead of the retirements
optionC: Reduce sampling and flushing schedules so the remaining operators can cover all other work
optionD: Assign the retiring operators extra overtime so no new hiring is needed before they leave

question: A district metered area still shows high night flow after several leak repairs. What is the best next data step?
correctAnswer: Compare night flow by subzone to narrow down where the remaining loss is located
explanation: Breaking the district into subzones and comparing night flows points crews toward the part of the network where losses remain.
options: Replace every customer meter in the district before doing any further flow analysis
Average the night flow over the full year so the high readings carry less weight
Compare night flow by subzone to narrow down where the remaining loss is located
Stop night flow monitoring in that district and rely on customer reports of leaks

optionB: Average the night flow over the full year so the high readings carry less weight

question: A pressure zone shows high pressures at night when demand is low. What is the best pressure management action to review first?
correctAnswer: Review pressure reducing valve settings against the night demand pattern in that zone
explanation: Night pressures rise as demand falls, so checking pressure reducing valve settings against night conditions is the logical first review.
options: Open a boundary valve to the higher neighbouring zone and leave it open for the whole night period
Increase the storage tank overflow elevation so more water can be held overnight
Ask customers in the zone to shift most of their water use into the night hours
Review pressure reducing valve settings against the night demand pattern in that zone

optionB: Increase the storage tank overflow elevation so more water can be held overnight
optionC: Ask customers in the zone to shift most of their water use into the night hours
optionD: Review pressure reducing valve settings against the night demand pattern in that zone

question: A neighbouring municipality requests emergency supply above the volume in its agreement. What should the overall responsible operator do first?
correctAnswer: Check the agreement terms and confirm available system capacity before committing supply
explanation: The agreement and actual capacity govern what can be supplied, so both are confirmed before a commitment is made.
options: Open the interconnect at full capacity and sort out the paperwork after the event ends
Check the agreement terms and confirm available system capacity before committing supply
Refuse the request outright because emergency volumes were not listed hour by hour
Promise the full requested volume so the neighbour can announce it to its customers
optionA: Open the interconnect at full capacity and sort out the paperwork after the event ends
optionB: Check the agreement terms and confirm available system capacity before committing supply
optionC: Refuse the request outright because emergency volumes were not listed hour by hour
optionD: Promise the full requested volume so the neighbour can announce it to its customers

question: Renewal costs are rising faster than water rates in a multi year forecast. What is a sound financial planning response?
correctAnswer: Phase projects by risk and update the long term forecast and reserve plan to match
explanation: Phasing by risk and keeping the forecast and reserves current spreads the funding need honestly instead of hiding it.
options: Remove the highest risk projects from the forecast so the totals appear balanced
Fund all renewal from one year of operating surplus regardless of the project size
Phase projects by risk and update the long term forecast and reserve plan to match
Stop updating the forecast until construction prices settle back to earlier levels
optionA: Remove the highest risk projects from the forecast so the totals appear balanced
optionB: Fund all renewal from one year of operating surplus regardless of the project size
optionC: Phase projects by risk and update the long term forecast and reserve plan to match

question: A utility compares its break rate per 100 km of main with a peer utility that reports a lower rate. Before copying the peer program, what should the manager check?

Whether the peer utility uses the same colour coding on its construction drawings
How many staff the peer utility assigns to answering customer billing questions
The peer utility average response time for routine meter reading route problems

explanation: Lining and replacement differ in life, risk, disruption and whole life cost, and a sound choice weighs all four together.

Remaining life, failure risk, disruption and whole life cost for each of the two options
The number of residents who attended the last public meeting about the project only
The age of the construction equipment each contractor plans to bring to the site

question: A cross training plan is built so vacations and sick days do not leave gaps. What outcome should the plan achieve?
correctAnswer: More than one qualified operator able to cover each critical operating task

Senior operators exempt from learning any task outside their original job posting
Training records kept informally so supervisors can adjust them without documentation

question: Pressure was lowered in a zone and complaints arrive from homes at high elevation. What is the best next step?

explanation: Local verification separates a true setting problem from valve or elevation effects before the whole zone is changed.
options: Raise pressure across the whole zone back to the earlier setting on the same day the complaints arrive
Tell the callers that pressure complaints are not recorded during a trial period
Verify local pressures and check for partially closed valves or elevation effects
Close the zone boundary valves so the high elevation area is fed from one main

optionD: Close the zone boundary valves so the high elevation area is fed from one main

question: Leakage fell after a pressure reduction, but fire flow at the zone fringe is questioned. What evaluation approach is strongest before settings are made permanent?

Review only the customer complaint counts recorded during the first trial month

question: Metering data will be used to justify a major capital request. What should leadership ensure before relying on it?
